title: Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic Transcription & hnRNA Processing
topic: RNA Polymerases I, II, III, 5'-Capping, 3'-Polyadenylation, & Splicing
quickSummary: Transcription: 3'->5' template strand copied into 5'->3' RNA. Prokaryotes: single core RNA Pol + Sigma-70 factor (-35/-10 Pribnow). Eukaryotes: RNA Pol I (rRNAs), Pol II (hnRNA/mRNA), Pol III (tRNA, 5S rRNA). hnRNA processing: 5'-Capping (7-mG 5'-5'), 3'-Polyadenylation (200-300 A residues), Splicing (Spliceosome removes introns, joins exons).

summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Transcription converts DNA into RNA. A transcription unit consists of a Promoter, Structural Gene, and Terminator. Prokaryotes use a single RNA polymerase with transient Sigma factor. Eukaryotes have 3 distinct RNA Polymerases (Pol I for rRNAs, Pol II for hnRNA/mRNA, Pol III for tRNA/5S rRNA). Eukaryotic pre-mRNA (hnRNA) undergoes 3 nuclear modifications: 5'-Capping (7-mG), 3'-Poly-A tail, and Splicing via Spliceosomes.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 6.1 Transcription Unit Architecture
- **Template (Antisense) Strand ($3' \rightarrow 5'$)**: The strand copied by RNA Polymerase.
- **Coding (Sense) Strand ($5' \rightarrow 3'$)**: Has the identical sequence as the synthesized RNA transcript (with $T$ replaced by $U$). Promoters and terminators are designated relative to the coding strand.

### 6.2 Prokaryotic vs. Eukaryotic Transcription Machinery

```
                     PROKARYOTIC TRANSCRIPTION INITIATION
                     
   Core RNA Polymerase (α₂ββ'ω) + Sigma Factor (σ⁷⁰)
                                       │
   Binds Promoter Sequences: -35 Region (TTGACA) & -10 Pribnow Box (TATAAT)
                                       │
   Unwinds DNA (Open Complex) ──► Discharges σ factor ──► Elongation proceeds
```

```
                        EUKARYOTIC RNA POLYMERASE TYPES
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                                 ▼                                 ▼
RNA POLYMERASE I                  RNA POLYMERASE II                 RNA POLYMERASE III
Transcribes 28S, 18S, 5.8S        Transcribes hnRNA / pre-mRNA      Transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA,
pre-rRNA in Nucleolus             (Inhibited by α-Amanitin)         and 7SL / snRNA
```

### 6.3 Post-Transcriptional Processing of Eukaryotic hnRNA

```
                         hnRNA PROCESSING CASCADE
                         
   1. 5'-CAPPING       ──► Addition of 7-Methylguanosine Triphosphate (7-mGPPP)
                           to 5' end via unusual 5'-5' triphosphate linkage.
                           
   2. 3'-POLYADENYLATION► Addition of 200–300 Adenylate residues (Poly-A Tail)
                           to 3' end catalyzed by Poly-A Polymerase.
                           
   3. SPLICING         ──► Removal of non-coding Introns and ligation of coding
                           Exons catalyzed by the Spliceosome (U1, U2, U4, U5, U6 snRNPs).
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Rho-Dependent vs Rho-Independent Termination
conceptBreakdown.title: Rho-Dependent vs Rho-Independent Termination
conceptBreakdown.content: In prokaryotes, intrinsic (Rho-independent) termination relies on a GC-rich stem-loop hairpin followed by a poly-U tract; Rho-dependent termination uses the hexameric ATP-dependent RNA helicase Rho (ρ) to unwind RNA-DNA hybrids.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Alternative Splicing and Proteomic Diversity
conceptBreakdown.title: Alternative Splicing and Proteomic Diversity
conceptBreakdown.content: Alternative splicing allows a single pre-mRNA to assemble exons in diverse combinatorial patterns, enabling ~20,000 human genes to generate over 100,000 distinct functional protein isoforms.
